title: PRD: Ingest handoff rubric and compatibility handoff for experimental open-model submissions
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: This PRD defines a narrow-scope intake rubric and machine-readable handoff contract for new open-model submissions (including ephemeral/experimental variants). The goal is to reduce back-and-forth between runtime, ops, and product teams by standardizing the metadata, compatibility annotations, and an automated preflight verification that runs at ingest time. This ticket clarifies requirements, scope changes from earlier drafts, and explicit acceptance criteria for beta rollout.
background: We continue to receive a high volume of open-model submissions with inconsistent metadata and vague compatibility notes. That ambiguity causes runtime rollouts to fail or requires manual intervention for pinning, fallback, and kernel selection. Existing intake heuristics are too permissive; reviewers spend hours confirming quantization compatibility, KV cache layout, and aliasing intents. This PRD proposes a minimal contract that gives the runtime deterministic signals for safe admission and staged rollout.
scope_changes: Narrowed to ingest-time metadata only (no UI catalog redesign in this ticket)
Removed automatic full-performance profiling — replaced with a lightweight runtime sanity probe
Added explicit requirement for a model-provided compatibility-token schema instead of freeform notes
requirements: Metadata schema: submissions must include 'compat_tags' (list), 'prov:source', 'recommended_pin' (semver-like string or 'none'), and 'alias' (optional) as machine-readable fields
Compat tags taxonomy: at minimum include 'kv-cache-safe' | 'quantized-safe' | 'attention-kernel-v2' | 'batchable' | 'streaming-friendly'

Ingest preflight: run a 3-step lightweight probe in the ingest pipeline that validates model load, tokenization round-trip for 200 tokens, and a single forward pass with random input to detect major shape mismatches
Handoff contract: catalog entry must publish a 'runtime-handoff' JSON URL pointing to pin recommendations, known incompatibilities, and preferred kernel hints
Pin semantics: allowed values are exact pin (e.g., 1.4.2), soft-pin (prefixed 'soft:'), or 'unforced' to indicate runtime may choose a compatible fallback
Alias policy: ephemeral experimental weights may declare an alias group; runtime will map aliases to stable fallbacks during overloads
Telemetry hooks: ingest must attach canonical eval prompt set identifiers and a minimal perf target (median latency per token expected) to the entry
Automated gating: entries with 'security_sensitive' flag require approval from Security team before being marked 'servable'
acceptance_criteria: Ingest pipeline schema accepted by catalog and runtime teams (sign-off from Runtime Eng + Product)
Automated preflight executes and returns a structured result for all new submissions in staging (success/fail + short logs)
Runtime honors 'recommended_pin' values for staged rollout in dedicated and private deployments during canary runs
At least two open-model submissions using the new handoff contract complete full ingest flow end-to-end in staging without manual reviewer edits
Docs: a short 'ingest checklist' markdown page exists in Confluence and is linked from the ingest UI
Security sign-off flow is documented and integrated with our intake — flagged items create a blocking Security review ticket automatically
open_questions: Should the ingest preflight run on dedicated GPU or cheaper CPU-only staging containers? Tradeoff between cost and fidelity.
What is the canonical list of compat tags we commit to for Q2? Proposed: kv-cache-safe, quantized-safe, streaming-friendly, unk-token-preserve
Do we enforce a maximum size for runtime-handoff JSON? (api simplicity vs expressiveness)
How will we surface soft-pins in the public catalog and in the SDK—expose verbatim or translate to runtime hints?
comments: 2026-03-11 Sofia Martinez: Draft posted to Confluence; requested runtime and security review. Added initial compat tag proposals.
2026-03-12 Priya Nair: Runtime prefers keeping preflight CPU-based for throughput reasons but wants optional GPU probe for quantization checks. Suggested adding 'probe_level' enum.

2026-03-13 Aisha Patel: Security needs a minimal checklist (no external network calls during preflight). Marked security_review_required=true and requested that the handoff JSON be scannable for exfil risks.
2026-03-14 Mateo Ruiz: Catalog team can accept the 'runtime-handoff' URL spec but asks to cap JSON at 64KB and limit embedded logs to links only.
2026-03-15 Liam Chen: Updated acceptance criteria to require two end-to-end staging ingests. Preparing two test model submissions this week.
notes: This ticket intentionally scopes only ingest-time behavior and metadata contracts. UI polish, large-scale profiling, and catalog search impact are out-of-scope and will be separate follow-ups. Keep the contract intentionally small: machine-readable tags + one runtime-handoff URL + a lightweight preflight probe.
